text:
This looks like early 2024. The fed funds rate is 5.33, which was in place from July 2023 to September 2024. Headline CPI at 3.11% matches January 2024 (3.1%), and core CPI at 3.87% also fits January 2024 (3.9%). The unemployment rate of 3.7% fits December 2023, but January 2024 was 3.7% as well.

Equity data supports a month-end of January or February 2024. The 12-month US equity return of 30% is consistent with the period ending January 2024 (around 20%) or February 2024 (around 30%). Equities returned +12.1% over 3 months, which fits the November–January window less well than the December–February window. The 1-month equity return of +3.5% suggests February (S&P was up 5.3% in February and 1.7% in January), so the figure is somewhat ambiguous.

Other cues point to February 2024. The 10-year yield at 4.27% fits end of February (4.25%), and the 2-year at 4.64% fits end of February (4.62%). Treasuries fell 1.3% in the month, which also fits February, when yields rose. Headline CPI of 3.11% fits January 2024 data, which was the latest published in February. Payrolls averaging 289k reflect the large upward revisions, with Dec, Jan and Feb all strong. That fits February 2024.

The 1-month equity return of 3.5% is a little low versus the S&P's 5.3% for February, but the figures may be adjusted. I'm going with February 2024.
